There are a few different issue

Critical mass: One of the greatest challenges with these sites is simply getting them started. No-one wants to contribute to a site until they can see that the site has other people contributing because: 1) they are getting things out, instead of just putting them in 2) they can see the site has some kind of future. Voat appears to have cleared this first bar, which is positive for its future outlook.

Market is naturally suited towards multiple players This isn't a winner takes all market. The larger the site gets, the bigger the issues of spam get, the more incentive people have to cheat the system, the more popular subs head towards the "lowest common denominator". Just as Reddit's natural equilibrium is some huge default Reddit's, plus lots of higher quality, smaller sub-reddits, the natural equilibrium for this market is one big player and multiple smaller players.

Differentiation over time Since this market has been dominated by Reddit for so long, the amount of innovation in this market has been limited and barely explored. As an example of what has already been done: the daily voting limits provide one method of improving what posts make it to the top, the chat boxes are very interesting too. The Reddit enhancement suite provides another source of ideas.

I think it will be to Reddit as 8chan is to 4chan. It will always have fewer users, but it will still have enough. And the users that are here should be better than the ones that stayed, because we are aware of the mistakes that destroyed Reddit.
